thesis: AST SpaceMobile is the purest bet on direct-to-smartphone satellite broadband: 50+ mobile network operator partners representing ~3 billion subscribers (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten, stc), $1.2B in contracted partner commitments, ~$3.5B cash, and a target of ~45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by end of 2026. FY2026 revenue guidance is only $150-200M against a ~$33B market cap, so the stock trades almost entirely on constellation execution and 2027+ monetization. The +31% week was largely sympathy momentum (Rocket Lab-Iridium acquisition read-across), not a fundamental change.
catalysts: BlueBird satellite launch cadence toward ~45 in orbit by end of 2026; BlueBird 1-5 full operational status gates carrier revenue
Initial intermittent US service targeted in 2026 with AT&T/Verizon; first substantial MNO revenue recognition
Further prepayments/commitments on the $1.2B contracted partner base ($175M stc prepayment already received)
US Government revenue stream expansion (already a named FY2026 revenue driver)
Sector momentum: Rocket Lab-Iridium $8B deal repricing space connectivity assets
risk_factors: Funding: full global constellation requires 100+ more satellites; if capital markets tighten, dilution or delay follows despite ~$3.5B cash (Q1 2026 net loss $191M)
Launch risk: a single failure carrying multiple Block 2 satellites causes multi-quarter delay and capital loss
Unproven at scale: interference management and handoffs across a 243-satellite fleet under full commercial load is an unsolved engineering problem
Competition: Starlink direct-to-cell and carrier alternatives could compress wholesale economics before AST reaches scale
Regulatory: FCC decisions and per-country landing rights are ongoing gating items
Valuation: ~165x FY2026 guided revenue; beta 2.72 with a +31% week that can unwind as fast as it arrived
